baseline:
B
The attention mechanism allows a model to weigh the importance of different parts of the input, selectively focusing on the most relevant information to make a decision or generate an output, much like how a human pays attention to specific words in a sentence to understand it.

B
Traditional sequence-to-sequence models compress the entire input sequence into a single fixed-size context vector. This becomes an information bottleneck for long sequences, causing the model to forget information from earlier parts of the input. The attention mechanism solves this by allowing the model to look back at the entire input sequence and focus on the most relevant parts when generating each output token.

C
The attention mechanism dynamically calculates and assigns importance scores (weights) to input tokens, allowing the model to focus on the most relevant parts of the input when generating a specific output.

B
The dot product is calculated between the Query vector of one token and the Key vectors of all tokens to measure their similarity, which forms the basis of the attention scores.

B
Self-attention allows every token in an input sequence to directly interact with every other token in parallel, which enables the model to capture long-range dependencies and is more efficient for modern hardware than the sequential processing of traditional models like RNNs.
